primary_meaning: Jesus Christ as the sacrificial Lamb of God whose death atones for sin
primary_basis: John 1:29, 36 (Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world)
1 Peter 1:18-19 (redeemed by the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish)
Isaiah 53:7 (suffering servant led like a lamb to the slaughter, read christologically)

alternatives.meaning: General symbol of innocence, meekness, or gentleness (sometimes applied to believers or as a moral quality rather than specifically to Christ's atonement)
basis: Luke 10:3; Matthew 10:16 (disciples sent as lambs among wolves)
Broader pastoral and prophetic lamb imagery

alternatives.meaning: The Passover or temple sacrificial lamb understood primarily in its original Israelite cultic sense, without necessary reference to Jesus
basis: Historical-critical readings that stop at OT cult

alternatives.meaning: Apocalyptic or messianic conqueror figure emphasizing victory and judgment more than (or instead of) substitutionary sacrifice
basis: Revelation's Lamb who opens seals, wages war, and rules (e.g., Rev 6; 17:14)

alternatives.meaning: Literal animal or non-christological metaphor with no fixed doctrinal load
basis: Ordinary pastoral references in OT narrative and poetry

notes: In mainstream historic Christian teaching and biblical interpretation, 'the Lamb' (especially capitalized or in titular use) overwhelmingly denotes Jesus Christ in his atoning, paschal role, integrating OT sacrifice typology with NT fulfillment texts. Alternative emphases exist but rarely displace this core identification in confessional or standard exegetical literature.
